title: Decoherence Cartography with Transportable Matter and Antimatter Qubits as Probes of Beyond the Standard Model Sectors
content: We propose a transport-enabled program of decoherence cartography: the inference of environment-conditioned decoherence functionals for a localized stored charged-particle qubit across distinct laboratory sites after controlling for measured technical noise. The framework is formulated generically for transportable matter and antimatter qubits, while being motivated in particular by recent progress in coherent spectroscopy of a single antiproton spin and by the physical transport of trapped antiprotons in a portable cryogenic Penning-trap. For each site and control sequence, we formulate the experiment as a hierarchical null test in which the measured coherence of the localized qubit is decomposed into a nuisance contribution predicted from monitored magnetic, vibrational, thermal, timing, and control channels, together with a residual environment-conditioned functional. In the conservative null model, transport and relocation induce only deterministic phases and standard open-system dephasing fixed by measured spectra. A residual signal that remains stable under revisits, control sequence changes, and site permutations would define an irreducible site-dependent decoherence effect and motivate targeted follow up searches for new physics, manifested in beyond the Standard Model and cosmology-motivated sectors. We formulate the operational observables, filter-function framework, identifiability conditions, dictionary examples, and benchmark sensitivities required to render both null and non-null outcomes interpretable.
